correctness.rationale: Conditional independence gives the exact identity Δ=-Kβ[2A−β(A+(K−1)B)]. The exact interference quotient maximum is the top eigenvalue of a positive two-by-two Gram matrix and its eigenvector meets the greedy ordering constraint. Residual coercivity establishes geometric mean-square convergence strictly inside the computed bound. At the bound and above it, explicit attainable residual ratios show equality and growth. Pure greedy two-worker unit-relaxation updates are orthogonal reflections off a measure-zero set of tied-residual initial states. Critical identities and examples were checked with the packaged stdlib script (2,000 exact rational moment cases and 5,000 numerical tests).

value.rationale: The exact stability design problem is motivated by concurrent stale residual selection, which was experimentally observed to have an aggressiveness-dependent cliff in Coleman (2026). The sharp formula isolates concurrency K, row coherence c, and exploration θ in a single natural interference eigenvalue. Especially substantive is the full-step K=2 bifurcation: pure greed repeats one stale projection twice, becoming an isometry for almost every start, while arbitrarily little uniform exploration restores global geometric mean-square convergence. This is neither a routine restatement of a sequential Kaczmarz bound nor an arbitrary numerical slice; it is a complete sharp classification of the smallest nontrivial shared-snapshot model with a concrete algorithm-design implication.
